_comment: Default copy for the SECOND questionnaire email: the one sent to people whose first
invitation carried a link they could not open.
A separate variant rather than an edit to the normal copy, because both are needed at the
same time. Fifty-one people are owed a working link; everyone else has heard nothing from
us at all and must not be told we broke something they never saw.
IT LEADS WITH THE ASK, NOT THE APOLOGY, and that is deliberate. Open tracking is off on the
sending domain, so we do not know who opened the first email - for most of these people we
would be apologising for something they never noticed. A subject line about a broken link
also reads as a system notification and opens worse than a question about their test. So
the fault is acknowledged in one plain sentence at the top and the rest is the ordinary
invitation, word for word, from surveyEmailDefaults.json.
Same placeholders as that file: {{name}}, {{button}}, {{link}}. The unsubscribe line is
appended by the sender and cannot be edited away here. The token in the link is the SAME one
their first email carried, so anyone who kept that email and tries it later still lands on
subject: How did your CBAT go? (working link this time)
heading: How did it go?
subtitle: {{name}}, six questions and about a minute. The link works this time.
body:
Hello {{name}},

We emailed you about this a few days ago and the link in it was broken. That was our fault, and this one works.

You trained with SkyWatch for a while, and then things went quiet. That usually means one thing: you have sat the real test.

If that is you, would you tell us how it went?

- Your answers go straight back into the training, so whoever is revising right now gets a better version than you had. What matched, what did not, and what we should fix.
- If you passed, we will record it. A PASSED badge then appears beside your name on every leaderboard.
- Six questions, about a minute, nothing to sign in to. The link below is yours alone.

{{button}}

Not sat it yet? Say so on the first question and we will leave you alone until after your test. Good luck with it.

Thanks,
The SkyWatch Team
